references.text: [ref:Joh 3:16|John 3:16] is the immediate context: Whoever believes in God's only Son shall not perish but have eternal life. Verse 18 elaborates on this by explaining that whoever believes is not condemned, while whoever does not believe has already been condemned.
[ref:Joh 3:36|John 3:36] repeats the same principle: Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, but whoever refuses to believe in the Son will not see life, for God's wrath remains on him.
[ref:Joh 5:24|John 5:24] confirms that whoever hears Jesus' word and believes in the one who sent him has eternal life and will not be condemned but has passed from death to life.
[ref:Joh 6:40|John 6:40] emphasizes that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him shall have eternal life – consistent with the promise that the believer is not condemned.

[ref:Joh 20:31|John 20:31] summarizes the entire purpose of the Gospel of John: that readers may believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and by believing have life in his name. The expression "in his name" connects directly to John 3:18 about believing in the name of God's only Son.

[ref:Apg 4:12|Acts 4:12] points out that there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved – parallel to believing in the name of God's only Son.
[ref:Rom 8:1|Romans 8:1] states that there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, which corresponds directly to the fact that whoever believes in him is not condemned.
[ref:Rom 8:34|Romans 8:34] asks who can condemn, since Christ Jesus is the one who died and was raised – a confirmation that the believer is free from judgment.

[ref:1 Joh 5:10-13|1 John 5:10–13] speaks of believing in the name of God's Son and that whoever does not believe God has made him a liar, because they have not believed the testimony God gave about his Son. The parallel to not believing in the name of the only Son in John 3:18 is clear.

[ref:Joh 1:12|John 1:12] says that all who received him, he gave the right to become children of God, those who believe in his name. Belief in Jesus' name as saving is a recurring theme in John's writings.

[ref:Joh 1:14|John 1:14] introduces the term "only begotten" (μονογενής): The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us, and we have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father. This is the background for the expression "the name of God's only Son" in John 3:18.

[ref:Joh 12:48|John 12:48] says that whoever rejects Jesus and does not accept his words has one who will judge him: the word that Jesus spoke will judge him on the last day. This elaborates on the idea that whoever does not believe is already condemned.
